fare38Total.reason: 57 business + 8 leisure passengers = 65; demand curves and strategy calculations are unchanged.

retiredWarnings.segmentation: The observed-data table has an internal inconsistency at fare $38: total tickets are listed as 60, but the type counts 57 and 8 add to 65. These entries are preserved as printed; the worked pricing calculations use the stated fitted curves.
retiredWarnings.pottery: Each bowl uses 4 lb of clay and each mug uses 3 lb, so clay usage is \(4x_1+3x_2\). At (5,10), this is 50 lb, not 70. Keep both product variables in the clay constraint.
retiredWarnings.fertilizer: The phosphate constraint is \(4x_1+3x_2\ge24\), using the phosphate supplied by both fertilizer types.
retiredWarnings.objective-range: Use the clay constraint \(4x_1+3x_2\le120\), consistent with 4 lb per bowl and 3 lb per mug. Repeating the second variable in both terms would describe a different resource constraint.
retiredWarnings.labor-shadow: Keeping the same solution mix preserves the current basis/product pattern, not the numerical quantities (24,8). At a range endpoint, a basic variable can become zero.
retiredWarnings.new-product: Willow Valley labor availability is uncertain, so retain \(H\) as a parameter and distinguish the examples with 40 and 65 hours. Each bowl uses 2 labor hours; using 1 would describe a different factory.
retiredWarnings.spreadsheet: Use 4 and 3 as the bowl and mug clay coefficients. The corresponding optimum is (24,8), with profit 1,360. A clay row containing only the mug variable is a different model.
retiredWarnings.solver-benchmarks: Benchmark values and vendor classifications below reproduce a dated course snapshot. They have not been presented as current release information or independently verified performance claims.
retiredWarnings.copt: The older Chapter 3 screenshots still use \(4x_{2} + 3x_{2} \le  120\) and return (40,0), \(Z = 1,600\). That solves the mistyped model. The separate COPT tutorial corrects the row to \(4x_{1} + 3x_{2} \le  120\) and reports (24,8), \(Z = 1,360\).
retiredWarnings.shirts: This is a derived continuous formulation. Quantities are measured in dozens; requiring whole dozens would add integer restrictions.
retiredWarnings.diet: This is a derived continuous model: fractional servings are allowed, and every food uses the serving unit listed in the data table. Whole-serving requirements would add integer restrictions.
retiredWarnings.portfolio: The model-summary page 9 is visibly blank beneath its headings. These equations follow from the table on page 8; they are not visible equations from page 9.
retiredWarnings.advertising: This formulation assumes divisible advertising quantities. Requiring whole advertisements adds integer restrictions and can change the optimum.
retiredWarnings.transport: Warehouse supplies are upper bounds and unused stock has no modeled penalty. A zero-cost dummy destination is an alternative representation of the 100-unit supply surplus.
retiredWarnings.blending: This is a derived formulation and optimum. Grade totals are fixed at the optimum, but component allocations can be nonunique.
retiredWarnings.production: The derived minimum cost of $216,300 assumes zero initial and terminal inventory, on-time demand, no backlogs, and storage charged between weeks.
retiredWarnings.pet-food: Page 24 is visibly blank beneath its model-formulation heading. The ingredient-allocation model and $1,992 worked optimum are derived from page 23. The stated per-can profits are used directly.
retiredWarnings.cash-flow: This model assumes project D matures after one year, percentage returns are added to repaid principal, and cash can be reinvested at year boundaries. These timing assumptions determine which investments are feasible.
retiredWarnings.dea: The CCR formulation assumes constant returns to scale. Different returns-to-scale conventions or restrictions on weights give different efficiency models and can change scores.
retiredWarnings.uncertain-returns: Page 32 leaves 38.33% of B’s probability mass unspecified. Do not invent a missing outcome, silently renormalize the two printed probabilities, or claim a unique stochastic optimum from the incomplete probabilities.
retiredWarnings.a2-claims: The official key’s page-3 chart swaps the coordinates of the workstation/error corner: it should be (34.444444,5.555556), not (5.55,34.45). Its optimum cost label $1,735.97 should round to $1,735.98. These corrections follow direct substitution into the printed model. The same chart’s nonoptimal-corner cost shown as $2,437.9 is $2,437.777778, or $2,437.78 to cents.
retiredWarnings.a3-bradley: The official key’s “corn >= $520” condition means all-corn is an optimal plan, not necessarily the only optimal plan. Uniqueness requires a strict increase above $520.
